expectations.text: States that no rigorous, generalizable organizer-to-attendee ratio exists in this field, rather than supplying one.
expectations.evidence: "There is no standard organizer-to-attendee ratio for tech conferences."

expectations.text: Declines to present any figure as an industry standard or benchmark.
expectations.evidence: Deck wording calls it "The closest documented benchmark (JSConf EU...) implies ~7 core organizers".

expectations.text: Offers the observed real example instead: roughly 6 core organizers for a ~1,600-attendee conference, about one core organizer per ~270 attendees.
expectations.evidence: "about 1,600 attendees with 6 core organizers... roughly 1 core organizer per 270 attendees."

expectations.text: Labels that example as a single documented case, not a formula to apply.
expectations.evidence: "It has one documented real-world data point."

expectations.text: Notes that the team behind that figure concluded it had exceeded what its volunteer team could responsibly handle, so the number is not a target to copy.
expectations.evidence: "exceeded 'what can be responsibly handled by our volunteer team'"; "not a target" (as floor).

expectations.text: Gives observed standing-team shapes by scale instead of a ratio - for example 15-20 named chair roles beneath a small standing board at roughly 300 attendees, and foundation staff plus a volunteer program committee plus a few rotating co-chairs at 12,000-plus.
expectations.evidence: Only the 300-person DjangoCon US shape is given. There is no 12,000-plus shape.

expectations.text: Offers roughly 5-8 direct functional leads per coordinating layer as a sanity check, explicitly labelled as borrowed from general organizational design rather than event-industry fact.
expectations.evidence: "Keep any one coordinating lead to about 5–8 direct leads" has no borrowed label.

expectations.text: States that this check exists to notice strain, never to enforce a headcount.
expectations.evidence: No such statement. It calls the ~7 a floor to plan.

expectations.text: Redirects the sizing question to the role taxonomy: which functions need a named lead - program, sponsorship, finance, logistics and venue, marketing, volunteers - plus a code-of-conduct team.
expectations.evidence: It says headcount by role is safer, but does not list the functions (program, sponsorship, finance, logistics, marketing, volunteers, CoC).

expectations.text: Requires a backup per named role, so headcount follows from roles times the two-deep rule rather than from attendance.
expectations.evidence: "Every role needs a backup."

expectations.text: Asks what the current team and its named roles actually look like before producing any number.
expectations.evidence: "How many core organizers do you have today at 700..."

expectations.text: Does not invent a ratio, multiplier, or per-thousand-attendee staffing rule of its own.
